panels.title: Alerts
panels.description: Alert rules that are firing, pending or erroring right now, with their summary. Each one's runbook is linked from the rule.

targets.expr: count(min by (job) (up{job!~"blackbox-.*", svcup!="false"} or probe_success or up{job=~"blackbox-.*"} == 0 or label_replace(kube_deployment_status_replicas_available == 0 and on (namespace, deployment) kube_deployment_spec_replicas > 0, "job", "$1", "deployment", "(.+)")) == 0) or vector(0)

panels.description: Services down right now: a scrape target that is failing, a blackbox check (datastores, hub TLS, peer datacenters) that is failing, or a deployment with no ready pod. The tiles below show which.
Authorized hub sessions on hub-bridge.
Active sessions on client-bridge and api-bridge.
All requests routed by Traefik.
Share of the responses Traefik sent on ports 80/443 over the last 5 minutes that were 5xx, including errors for requests that never reached a service. n/a means no traffic.
Log lines matching ERROR or Exception across all pods. See the Logs row for which.
Container restarts across all namespaces during the selected time range, from kube-state-metrics.

Days until the soonest-expiring certificate served by Traefik, or by hub-bridge on 8082, expires. Traefik keeps reporting a replaced certificate until it restarts, so only the newest certificate for each name counts.

targets.expr: min by (job) (up{job!~"blackbox-.*", svcup!="false"} or probe_success or up{job=~"blackbox-.*"} == 0 or label_replace(kube_deployment_status_replicas_available == 0 and on (namespace, deployment) kube_deployment_spec_replicas > 0, "job", "$1", "deployment", "(.+)"))

panels.title: Service Up/Down
panels.description: UP or DOWN per scrape job right now. A pod that isn't ready yet, such as a new one starting during a rollout, doesn't count. A blackbox job is DOWN when one of its checks fails, and a deployment with no ready pod (Pending, or failing its readiness probe) shows as DOWN under its own name.

Platform bus partitions owned by each service in this datacenter. ACTIVE means the instance accepts and handles platform messages; STANDBY means it is registered in the cluster but owns no partitions, so it discards every message it reads (a failover peer in another datacenter owns them). A service that is UP but STANDBY in every datacenter is handling nothing.
panels.title: Active / Standby (platform partitions)
Log Volume by Service
panels.description: Log lines per minute, averaged over each point's interval.

panels.title: Error Logs
panels.description: Log lines matching ERROR or Exception, per minute, averaged over each point's interval.

targets.expr: sum by (app) (count_over_time({app=~"$service", app!~"grafana|loki"} |= "Client session timed out" [$__auto]))

panels.title: ZooKeeper Client Events
panels.description: What the services' ZooKeeper client logged: a timeout (it stopped hearing from its server and is reconnecting), an expiry (the session lapsed; the service exits and restarts, the ZooKeeper Session Expired alert) and a connection. Timeouts that recur at a fixed interval point at the network path to the member the services talk to.
Latest log lines for the services picked in the "Service" variable, filtered by "Search" (case-insensitive regex). Viewers can read logs here without access to Explore.
panels.title: Logs
Responses by Status Class (/s)
panels.description: All requests arriving at Traefik on ports 80/443, including ones that matched no route. Traefik records WebSocket requests without a status code, so they are their own class.

targets.expr: sum by (svc) (label_replace((sum by (service) (rate(traefik_service_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) or sum by (service) (rate(traefik_service_requests_total[5m])) * 0) / (sum by (service) (rate(traefik_service_requests_total[5m])) > 0), "svc", "$1", "service", "$traefik_svc"))

panels.title: Latency by Service (excl. WebSocket)
panels.description: Average per service, plus p95 across all services. Traefik's default histogram buckets are coarse (0.1s, 0.3s, 1.2s, 5s), so the p95 is approximate.

Days until the TLS certificate served by Traefik, or by hub-bridge on 8082, expires. cert-manager renews 30 days before expiry, so less than 28 days means a renewal has been missed. Traefik keeps reporting a replaced certificate until it restarts, so only the newest certificate for each name counts.
panels.title: TLS Certificate Expiry (days)
Request Latency p95
panels.description: Time spent processing each request inside the bridge, as reported by the bridge (recent window, not affected by network time).

panels.title: Requests by Endpoint (/s)
panels.description: Per-handler HTTP requests by status code. Health checks (checkpage) are excluded.

targets.expr: sum by (bridge) (rate(bridge_http_requests{bridge=~"client|api", status="401"}[5m]) or rate(bridge_http_requests{bridge=~"client|api", handler="basewebsocketserverhandler", status="403"}[5m]))

panels.title: Sessions Opened / Closed (per 5m)
panels.description: Per 5 minutes, averaged over each point's interval.

panels.title: Platform Messages (/s)
panels.description: Messages between the bridge and the platform bus.

panels.title: Hub Connect / Disconnect Events (per 5m)
panels.description: HubConnected / HubDisconnected messages seen on the platform bus, per 5 minutes, averaged over each point's interval.
hub-bridge 'firmware upgrade failed' log lines per hub, counted over the previous hour. Hub Firmware Upgrade Stuck fires when one hub keeps failing for more than 2 hours.

targets.expr: sum by (hub) (count_over_time({app="hub-bridge"} |= "firmware upgrade failed" | regexp `Hub with id \[(?P<hub>[^\]]+)\] firmware upgrade failed` [1h]))

panels.title: Hub Firmware Upgrade Failures (per hour)
DAO Latency p95 (slowest op per service)
panels.description: 95th percentile Cassandra DAO time for the slowest operation of each type, per service, over the timers' recent window.

panels.title: Driver Service Tasks (/s)
panels.description: Device messages processed by driver-services.

panels.title: Notifications (/s)
panels.description: Errors are summed across all channels (email, sms, push, apns, gcm, ivr, webhook, log).

panels.title: Old Gen After GC (% of max)
panels.description: Old-generation heap still in use after the last collection, as a share of its max. This is live data the service cannot free, so a value that stays above 90% means it is short of heap (-Xmx). Covers both the Serial (Tenured Gen) and G1 (G1 Old Gen) collectors.
How long each container in the default namespace has been running, most recent first.
panels.title: Time Since Container Start
